Processing historical documents using natural-language processing becomes challenging due to numerous spelling variations and sparse annotation of available data. A prevalent method involves these terms being standardized to match their contemporary written forms. This study investigates the viability of a neural network architecture designed for such tasks, with specific application to a Character-level deep bi-directional LSTM (deep bidirectional recurrent neural network). The results of evaluations across a wide variety of texts derived from the Old Modern High German indicate strong performance when compared to established normalization algorithms. We further demonstrate that advanced multi-task training, incorporating additional normalization data capable of enhancing our model performance and refining accuracy in predicted outputs, yields superior results in classification tasks compared to previous methods established in historical data normalization algorithms.

Therefore, research continues to explore whether deep learning-based methods outperform existing rule-based systems by significantly improving both speed and accuracy while addressing issues specific to historical texts containing

We investigate a stochastic SIR (Susceptible-Infectious-Removed) epidemic on a configuration model random graph where infectious nodes transmit to graph neighbors over varying duration defined by any specific but fixed distribution. Under the assumption that node degrees are bounded, we establish central limit theorems governing the final size of the infection (representing the initial susceptibles that become infected) in terms of the explicit and tractable expressions for asymptotic variances, valid for large population sizes ($n$). These findings apply to two settings of the random graph structure: deterministic degree sequences for the Molloy-Reed graph and independent, identically distributed degree sequences for the Newman-Strogatz-Watts graph. The theorems address both scenario (a), where the initial fraction of infectious nodes converges to a limit (potentially zero), including when $n$ approaches infinity, and scenario (b), where a finite number of individuals initiate infection as $n$ approaches infinity, requiring results conditional upon the emergence of a major outbreak (specifically one of scale exceeding logarithMIC $n$). Furthermore, results regarding the distribution of the largest cluster under both bond percolation for these specific graph models and standard percolation are derived as immediate corollaries, alongside central limit theorems for the size of the largest connected component, including proofs for the case of site percolation.

Robot manipulators deployed in logistics and manufacturing often function in semi-structured spaces alongside humans and other machines. While these settings are predominantly stationary, movable obstacles occasionally arise that the robots must navigate around. Such manipulation tasks typically involve significant repetition yet demand rapid and dependable motion planning to meet tight timing requirements. Initial preprocessing strategies excel in highly structured layouts, yet they struggle when movable obstacles appear, given that these elements remain unmodeled beforehand. In response, we present an innovative preprocessing technique named the Alternative Paths Planner (APP), designed to ensure planning performance with provable fixed-time guarantees in semi-structured domains. APP pre-constructs a library of diverse alternative paths offline so that, regardless of how movable obstacles configure, a collision-free trajectory always exists within this collection for any given scenario. Once deployed for actual use, a valid collision-free path can be retrieved almost instantly within mere microseconds. Assessing APP on a seven-degrees-of-freedom robotic arm across semi-structured domains of diverse complexities showed that it is orders of magnitude quicker than current best-in-class motion planners. This methodology was further confirmed through real-time testing on a physical manipulator.

Our results demonstrate that large gauge transformations alter momentum conservation rules, yielding nonzero three-point amplitudes even within a simple model of gravitational wave emission. This effect clarifies an apparent conflict between exact field-theory approaches and perturbative amplitude calculations. When large gauge contributions are incorporated using an adjusted LSZ formulation, the tension disappears at all loop orders; without these effects, perturbative approximations capture only a fraction of the full non-perturbative result. While our study uses specific models for derivation, the core concepts parallel dynamical gravitational scattering scenarios.

Logarithmic conformation reformulations of viscoelastic constitutive equations have addressed the high Weissenberg number barrier, rendering the simulation of highly elastic flows feasible. Despite this, their application within the finite element context lacks extensive stabilization methods for direct solution. This study proposes stabilized formulations for the Saramito (2013) logarithmic rearrangement of the Oldroyd-B model, utilizing both Galerkin/Least-Squares and Variational Multiscale approaches. Fully implicit characteristics in these reformulations enable direct solution via Newton methods for steady-state configurations. The devised strategies eliminate convective and compatibility instabilities while maintaining a three-field problem structure. Evaluations across the four-roll periodic benchmark demonstrated equivalent spatial accuracy between methods further confirmed by validation against flows involving 4:1 contraction and a cylinder. The sub-grid scale algebraic algorithm exhibits strong reliability even at elevated limiting Weissenberg numbers, aligning excellingly with established reference data.

Identifying atmospheric water vapor on temperate rocky exoplanets represents a critical step toward characterizing their habitability. Although earlier modeling suggests that cloud formation on Earth-like worlds with oceans could hinder detecting this vapor with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) due to blocked spectral signals using transit observations, a new analysis explores a more promising target: arid rocks worlds with frozen water poles or seas. Transit spectrum simulations indicate that H2O gas may be more readily detected on planets lacking dense atmospheric cloud decks. However, detecting these signals remains difficult, with remaining obstacles including line interference by gases like carbon dioxide and stellar water, absorption by surface mineral dust (extinction) if the planet lacks a thick haze, as well as JWST's own instrumental noise limits. Consequently, a combined suite of future astronomical measurements is indispensable for securing reliable confirmation of H2O.

The work explores sufficient criteria satisfied by specific weight distributions, such as radial, angular, and non-radial ones, that enable piecewise norm approximations utilizing analytic polynomials.

This work introduces a universal form of the optical theorem based on Localized Waves, a representation frequently utilized to produce Frozen waves, Xwaves, and other propagation-invariant beams. Furthermore, we examine multiple instances by employing diverse input sources detected circularly to determine the extinction cross-section.

In the realm of mobile edge computing, edge servers are strategically deployed in close geographical proximity to end-users and base stations to deliver highly efficient and accessible computing capabilities and services. Within this ecosystem, service providers may utilize leased edge servers to minimize the service latency experienced by their clients. An ideal deployment strategy aims to accommodate the maximum number of user allocations while simultaneously minimizing reliance on leased servers, all while strictly meeting user quality-of-service requirements. This paper models the edge user allocation problem as a bin-packing scenario and proposes a novel optimal solution grounded in Lexicographic Goal Programming. We evaluated the framework through three sets of experiments contrasting it with two established baseline methods. The experimental data indicate that our proposed approach delivers significantly superior performance compared to the competing solutions.

Detecting duplicate questions (DQD) is vital for improving the efficiency of automatic and community-driven QA systems. However, acquiring supervised data within a specific domain is costly and tedious, and utilizing annotations across different domains presents limitations. This paper addresses DQD cross-domain generalization using neural representations by analyzing nearest neighbors. The approach involves encoding question pairs from both source and target domains into an enriched representation space to rank new pairs based on aggregated neighbor labels and distances via a k-Nearest Neighbors retrieval technique. This method demonstrates strong robustness across various cross-domain scenarios in StackExchange, Spring, and Quora benchmarks, surpassing cross-entropy classification in several instances.

Prompt Tuning has grown as an effective, data- and parameter-efficient strategy for adapting large pretrained vision-language models to various downstream tasks. Yet, current techniques typically treat prompts for each task as entirely independent, overlooking vast shareable knowledge across the domain of vision-language tasks. In response, we introduce Multitask Vision-Language Prompt Tuning (MVLPT), which integrates cross-task knowledge directly into the prompt tuning workflow for these models. Specifically, we demonstrate that learning a single, transferable set of prompt vectors across multiple source tasks provides a powerful initialization for subsequent target tasks. Furthermore, we show that these targets can mutually benefit from shared prompt vectors, enabling them to be learned concurrently through multitask prompt tuning.

Extensive evaluations across three leading prompt tuning paradigms—text, visual, and unified text-vision approaches—reveal significant gains. Our benchmarks, covering 20 tasks, confirm that MVLPT surpasses single-task baselines, establishing new state-of-the-art results on both few-shot ELEVATER evaluations and cross-task generalization assessments to identify where the shared knowledge proves most effective. To dissect task transferability, we conducted a large-scale study evaluating 400 task pairs within 5 methods. Our analysis shows that peak performance for each prompt tuning variant relies on distinct task combinations, with mutual benefits driven largely by visual and label similarities between tasks. Addressing this in a digital-signal-based control framework, we introduce a novel discrete-time higher-order sliding mode controller integrated with time delay estimation (T DE). The dynamic model utilized in this approach enables effective management of competing complexities, such as parametric uncertainties handled by the TD S and system nonlinearity addressed via a tailored feedback structure:

The terminal sliding mode surface combined with the high-performance controller guarantees improved stability, reduced output ripple amplitude (chatter levels) at a smaller level, while ensuring robust transient response (fast convergence). The design also features a **variable**modified **sliding mode surface** (VSSMS) and enhanced **control gain structures** (VGCS); this significantly bolsters stability performance across diverse scenarios, allowing faster adaptation. Stability conditions are formally derived for the closed loop here. Simulation data and on-board experimental data confirm the system exhibits high-accuracy, robust operation despite complex disturbances/DOFs.

We have developed a simple prototype designed to detect short-duration optical transient events, utilizing the innovative tilt-shift imaging method detailed by Tingay (2020). This setup employs two synchronized cameras with a shared field-of-view nearing 3.7 square degrees, capturing more than 34,000 five-second exposures over a span of roughly twenty-four hours. With an effective pixel exposure duration of 21 milliseconds, the system is sensitive to optical flashes brighter than V magnitude 6.6 across 89.7 square degree hours of data; however, it detected no candidate astronomical transients. This result yields a limiting rate for such events of 0.8 occurrences per square degree per day, matching the performance of comparable instruments. False alarms, such as satellite artifacts or other instrumental noise, are readily distinguished by the dual-camera arrangement through reflection signatures. Future advancements will focus on scaling this promising approach toward larger aperture and broader viewing area systems.

The Internet now serves as a potent channel for the daily dissemination of a wide array of health data. Globally, searches related to symptoms, illnesses, medications, and other health topics are experiencing massive growth. Standard search engines generally base their results on a single user input, meaning finding relevant outcomes often demands extensive manual filtering. Existing search and recommendation systems currently fall short in offering real-time interactions necessary to produce more precise answers. This paper introduces an intelligence and interaction-capable system connected to extensive medical big data repositories, demonstrating its efficacy in locating specific healthcare information.

We demonstrate that the Loop O(1) model—a prominent graphical representation of the Ising model—is realizable as a factor of independent and identically distributed processes on unimodular random rooted graphs across several conditions, specifically including scenarios involving a non-negative external field. Consequently, we establish that the free Isig model's gradient forms a factor of independent and identically distributed processes on unimodular planar maps where the dual lattice has a structure locally finite by degree. Central to these results is the development and application of a theory concerning local limits of uniform bipartition sets under different boundary constraints, confirming that such limits can be realized as independent factors with product distributions. We also establish a key finding previously suggested to Hutchcroft as a conjecture-like problem, specifically that the wired uniform spanning tree over unimodular transient graphs behaves as a factor of independent and identically distributed processes.

Detecting novel object gripping capabilities in disordered environments represents a critical function of robotic manipulators. Whereas 2D tasks involving grasping restricted images often utilize fully convolutional neural networks to forecast grasping in a single step, such methods fail in grasp pose contexts where positions exist within SE3 rather than the 2D image plane. Consequently, this domain commonly adopts a dual-stage strategy of generating grasping candidates before classifying them; given the high cost associated with this second stage, the crucial aim becomes identifying top-grade grasping opportunities with high efficiency. This article introduces a novel technique for grasp candidate generation that decisively exceeds current leading 3D baselines. The supplementary content can be found at https://atenpas.github.io/psn/.

Since graph-derived datasets from real-world applications inevitably contain noise, practical graphical representations must be inherently resilient to such interference. While current investigations largely emphasize feature smoothing and often overlook geometric structural perturbations, most also depend on the L2-norm to enforce global smoothness, thereby constraining the expressive potential of graph neural networks (GNNs). This paper introduces regularizers specifically designed to mitigate both feature inconsistencies on attributes of graphs' structures, ensuring that we have a more robust model. We've found an efficient solution technique for the objective function using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Our approach removes over-smoothing concerns when expanding across multiple layers. Furthermore, it guarantees optimal convergence. The empirical results validate them in showing our model performs significantly more effectively than widely accepted graph convolutions in heavily contaminated settings.

This study investigates triangle decompositions in graphs by developing classes of instances where every edge resides within a triangle, such that attaching the smallest requisite quantity of double edges between existing neighboring vertices yields a strongly triangle divisible graph capable of triangle decomposition. The research analyzes diverse categories, including several planar classes and an area on torus graphs.

Despite existing knowledge regarding various allosteric regulation pathways, the intrinsic nature of the "allosteric signal" and its propagation timescale remain poorly understood. This study investigates the PDZ3 domain of the postsynaptic density-95 protein, characterized by an allosterically active C-terminal third $\alpha$-helix ($\alpha$3). By cross-linkeding the $\alpha$3 helix with an azobenzene group, we generated a photoswitchable PDZ3 variant. Upon photoswitching, the induced structural transitions alter the binding affinity of peptides for a distant pocket. Employing time-resolved infrared and UV/Visible spectroscopy, we have resolved the transmission of this allosteric signal, revealing that it traverses the entire protein structure in less than 200 nanoseconds.
